detail: No PubMed abstract reports BCKDHB variants in a patient with peripheral neuropathy. MSUD neuropathy leads: Kleopa 2001 Muscle Nerve (11180212, acute axonal neuropathy in MSUD; it says PN was 'not identified previously as a clinical feature of MSUD') and 18855118 (2008 JIMD, variant MSUD with sensorimotor polyneuropathy). Neither abstract gives the genotype and no PMC full text; web search found nothing linking BCKDHB variants to neuropathy. MSUD can be BCKDHA/BCKDHB/DBT, so gene assignment is unconfirmed. If curators accept MSUD-level evidence, the earliest is 11180212 (2001 Feb).

Accepted only because acute motor neuropathy is a recognised feature of acute hepatic porphyria attacks (HCP); the abstract does not document neuropathy in this patient. Martasek et al. 1994 HMG. The first explicit HCP neuropathy report is Muscle Nerve 1994 Jul (8008008, 'Acute peripheral neuropathy due to hereditary coproporphyria'), but it was diagnosed biochemically with no genotype. No abstract found that pairs a CPOX variant with documented PN. Downstream may prefer 'unverified'. | Round 2: only paper documenting neuropathy (35228944) reports a VUS; definition requires a pathogenic variant -> unverified.

Paper states it is the first identification of a causal FAH mutation. PN qualifies as a recognised feature of HT1 (acute porphyria-like neurologic crises with axonal peripheral neuropathy; Mitchell 1990 NEJM PMID 2153931), though not described in this abstract. Next mutation papers: Labelle 1993 (8364576), Grompe 1994 (8028615).

No PubMed record found reporting L1CAM variants in patients with documented peripheral neuropathy; peripheral neuropathy is not a recognised core feature of L1 syndrome (hydrocephalus/MASA/SPG1/CRASH). Gene appears via the HSP panel (SPG1). If the study treats complicated HSP genes as qualifying without documented PN, the first L1CAM-HSP paper is Jouet et al., Nat Genet 1994 Jul, PMID 7920659 ('X-linked spastic paraplegia (SPG1), MASA syndrome and X-linked hydrocephalus result from mutations in the L1 gene'); first L1CAM disease mutation overall: Rosenthal et al., Nat Genet 1992 Oct, PMID 1303258 (X-linked hydrocephalus). Muñoz et al. 2016 (PMID 26916325) CRASH cases explicitly had normal neurophysiology. Full-text case reports were not screened, so an incidental PN mention cannot be fully excluded.

No abstract documents peripheral neuropathy in SPART-mutation patients. Troyer syndrome's cardinal features are spastic paraparesis, pseudobulbar palsy and distal amyotrophy (lower motor neuron). Neuropathy is not stated. Candidate if distal amyotrophy is accepted as a motor neuropathy/neuronopathy: Patel 2002 Nat Genet (12134148, 2002 Aug, Amish Troyer syndrome). Others checked: 15372254, 18413476, 20437587, 27112432, 28679690.

Only Mendelian TRPA1 disease is familial episodic pain syndrome 1 (Kremeyer et al., Neuron 2010 Jun 10, PMID 20547126: N855S gain-of-function; 'Quantitative sensory testing demonstrated normal baseline sensory thresholds') -- a channelopathic pain disorder without documented neuropathy. Closest PN report: Sleczkowska et al., Int J Mol Sci 2022 Nov 15, PMID 36430572 -- 'potentially pathogenic' heterozygous TRPA1 variants in 7/414 painful small fiber neuropathy patients (cohort screening, VUS-level; not established pathogenic). If the study accepts SFN cohort variants, use 36430572 (2022, low confidence); if FEPS counts as PN-spectrum, use 20547126 (2010).

Discovery paper Valdmanis 2007 AJHG (17160902) describes 'relatively severe, pure spastic paraplegia' - no PN. No SPG8 abstract (2013-2021 case reports/series checked: 23455931, 23881105, 25454649, 26572744, 28181327, 29768361, 29907907, 31814071, 33662919) mentions neuropathy. Panel PMID 27164712 (Wang 2016 Neurology, polyneuropathy NGS panel) does not name WASHC5/KIAA0196 in abstract or PMC main text (supplement not checked). Ritscher-Schinzel/3C syndrome (24065355) has no PN. Recommend exclude unless a supplementary-table case is found.
